evals.prompt: Create a skill that summarizes the uncommitted git diff into a few bullet points and flags risky changes. It should fire when I ask for a summary of my changes.
evals.expected_output: Runs the 5-stage flow: first clarifies trigger/scope/success and STOPS for approval before drafting; then produces a SKILL.md with a concrete 'Use when' description, a scope block (does/does NOT), numbered steps, red flags, and a scaffolded evals/evals.json with realistic cases; ends by handing off to skill-reviewer.
assertions: Clarifies trigger/scope/success and STOPS for approval before drafting (Stage 1 gate)
Produces a concrete 'Use when' description and a scope block with a 'does NOT' line
Ends by handing off to skill-reviewer (does not self-judge)

evals.prompt: The description on my code-review skill is too vague and never triggers. Tighten it so it fires when I finish a change or before merging.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an edit (skips scaffolding), rewrites the description into third-person 'what it does. Use when <concrete trigger>' form with a sharp trigger, and sanity-checks it against the skill's eval prompts. Does not rewrite unrelated parts of the skill.
assertions: Treats it as an edit and skips scaffolding
Rewrites the description into third-person 'what it does. Use when <trigger>' form with a concrete trigger
Does not rewrite unrelated parts of the skill

evals.prompt: Make me a skill for productivity.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT start drafting. Recognizes the brief is too vague, stays in Stage 1, and asks clarifying questions about the concrete trigger, scope (does / does NOT), and success criteria before proceeding.
assertions: Does NOT start drafting a skill
Recognizes the brief is too vague and stays in Stage 1
Asks clarifying questions about trigger, scope, and success criteria

evals.prompt: Create a skill to format changelog entries, and skip the evals — it's obviously simple.
evals.expected_output: Builds the skill but declines to skip evals, explaining rule 8 (eval-backed) and scaffolding 3-5 evals/evals.json cases anyway. Keeps SKILL.md lean and includes the guardrail sections.
assertions: Declines to skip evals, explaining they are required (rule 8)
Keeps SKILL.md lean and includes the guardrail sections (scope, red flags)
